title: Zero-context insertions mishandle the unchanged line preceding the insertion
reasoning: For a unified insertion hunk such as @@ -5,0 +6,2 @@, old_start identifies the line before the insertion. The offset function applies the insertion delta to old line 5 even though that line stays at 5. The span containment check also treats the empty old range as overlapping a single-line grade at line 5, dropping that unchanged grade.
reproduction: Parse @@ -5,0 +6,2 @@ followed by two added lines. compute_line_offset(hunks, 5) returns (7, false), and is_span_unchanged(hunks, 5, null) reports changed; the line should remain unchanged at 5.
recommendation: Handle zero-length old ranges as insertion boundaries after old_start, and distinguish insertions inside a span from insertions immediately outside its endpoints.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: All included offset and span scenarios use positive old_count values; none exercise pure insertion boundaries.
suggestedRegressionTest: Extend offset and span scenarios with zero-context insertions before, inside, and after spans, including start-of-file and end-of-file insertions.
minimumFixScope: compute_line_offset, is_span_unchanged, and their existing behavioral test classes.

history.reasoning: Both evidence paths and symbols still exist.
